meta.title: American History Preview
meta.description: A taste of the Socratic method with Benjamin Franklin

questions.questionText: Who wrote the pamphlet 'Common Sense' that helped convince colonists to support independence?
questions.answerExplanation: Thomas Paine wrote 'Common Sense' in 1776. It sold hundreds of thousands of copies and persuaded many colonists that independence from Britain was necessary.
mnemonics: Paine = Pain-fully honest about why we needed independence

questions.questionText: What was the name of the first permanent English settlement in America?
questions.answerExplanation: Jamestown was founded in 1607, making it the first permanent English settlement. Plymouth came later in 1620.
mnemonics: James-town was first - J comes before P (Plymouth)

questions.questionText: The Boston Tea Party was a protest against what?

options.label: A
options.text: The price of tea being too high

questions.answerExplanation: The Boston Tea Party in 1773 protested taxation without representation. The colonists objected to paying taxes to a Parliament where they had no voice.
mnemonics: No taxation without representation - the rallying cry of revolution

questions.questionText: Which explorer's voyage in 1492 opened the Americas to European exploration?
questions.answerExplanation: Christopher Columbus sailed in 1492 and reached the Caribbean, opening sustained European contact with the Americas. While Vikings like Leif Erikson came earlier, Columbus's voyage led to permanent colonization.
mnemonics: In 1492, Columbus sailed the ocean blue

questions.questionText: Why did the Pilgrims leave England and come to America?
questions.answerExplanation: The Pilgrims were Separatists who wanted to worship freely without interference from the Church of England. Religious freedom was their primary motivation for the dangerous voyage.

questions.questionText: The Stamp Act of 1765 required colonists to pay taxes on what?

options.label: B
options.text: Printed materials like newspapers and legal documents

questions.answerExplanation: The Stamp Act required colonists to buy special stamps for all printed materials - newspapers, playing cards, legal documents, and more. It affected nearly everyone and sparked widespread protest.
mnemonics: Stamp = papers you STAMP approval on (documents, newspapers)

questions.questionText: What was the significance of the phrase 'No taxation without representation'?

options.label: B
options.text: Colonists believed they should have a voice in Parliament if they had to pay taxes

options.label: C
options.text: Colonists refused to pay any taxes at all

questions.answerExplanation: The phrase expressed the colonists' core grievance: they were being taxed by a Parliament in which they had no elected representatives. It was about political rights, not just money.
mnemonics: Representation = having a voice in decisions that affect you

questions.questionText: Why did Spain, Portugal, England, and France compete to explore and colonize the Americas?

options.label: B
options.text: To gain wealth, expand territory, and spread their religion

options.label: D
options.text: To learn from Native American cultures

questions.answerExplanation: European nations sought 'God, Gold, and Glory' - spreading Christianity, acquiring wealth through trade and resources, and expanding their empires for national prestige.
mnemonics: God, Gold, and Glory - the three Gs of exploration

questions.questionText: The Intolerable Acts were passed by Britain in response to what event?

options.label: A
options.text: The signing of the Declaration of Independence

questions.answerExplanation: The Intolerable Acts (1774) were Britain's punishment for the Boston Tea Party. They closed Boston Harbor and restricted colonial self-government, pushing the colonies closer to revolution.
mnemonics: Tea Party led to Intolerable punishment - Britain was NOT amused

questions.questionText: How did the geography of the New England colonies influence the economy there?

options.label: A
options.text: Rich soil led to large tobacco plantations

options.label: B
options.text: Rocky soil and harbors led to fishing, shipbuilding, and trade

options.label: C
options.text: Flat land led to cattle ranching

questions.answerExplanation: New England's rocky soil made large-scale farming difficult, but its coastline and forests made it ideal for fishing, shipbuilding, and trade. Geography shapes economy.
mnemonics: New England = rocky coast = ships and fish, not farms

questions.questionText: What document, signed in 1620 aboard a ship, established self-government in Plymouth Colony?
questions.answerExplanation: The Mayflower Compact was signed aboard the Mayflower in 1620. It was an early example of self-government, where the colonists agreed to make laws for the good of the colony.

questions.questionText: Why was the First Continental Congress significant in American history?

options.label: B
options.text: It was the first time colonies worked together to address their grievances with Britain

questions.answerExplanation: The First Continental Congress (1774) was groundbreaking because representatives from 12 colonies met to coordinate a response to British policies. It marked the beginning of colonial unity.

questions.questionText: The Columbian Exchange refers to the transfer of plants, animals, and diseases between which regions?
questions.answerExplanation: The Columbian Exchange was the widespread transfer of plants, animals, culture, and diseases between the Americas and the Old World (Europe, Africa, Asia) following Columbus's voyages.
mnemonics: Columbus = Columbian Exchange - Old World meets New World

questions.questionText: How did the French and Indian War contribute to tensions between Britain and the American colonies?

options.label: A
options.text: France gained control of the colonies

options.label: B
options.text: Britain's war debt led to new taxes on the colonies

options.label: C
options.text: The colonists wanted to remain loyal to France

options.label: D
options.text: Native Americans took over colonial governments

questions.answerExplanation: Britain won the French and Indian War but accumulated massive debt. To pay it off, Parliament imposed new taxes on the colonies, sparking protests that eventually led to revolution.
mnemonics: War costs money - Britain made colonies pay, colonies got angry

questions.questionText: What fundamental principle did the colonists believe the British government was violating?

options.label: B
options.text: The natural rights of life, liberty, and property

options.label: C
options.text: The right to form labor unions

options.label: D
options.text: The separation of church and state

questions.answerExplanation: Enlightenment thinkers like John Locke argued that all people have natural rights. The colonists believed British policies violated these fundamental rights, justifying their resistance.
mnemonics: Locke's locks: Life, Liberty, Property - keys to natural rights
